name: task-115-residual-matched-recall-latency-intel-local
comment: Task 115 Phase 5 MATCHED-RECALL latency confirmation. RUN ONLY AFTER Phase 4 (task-115-residual-recall-per-probe) shows residual improves recall-per-probe. NON-STANDARD config (justified): this is a matched-recall (not matched-nprobe) latency A/B — the whole product thesis is 'fewer probes for the same recall => lower latency', so each arm is pinned to the nprobe that hits the SAME recall@10 target read off the Phase-4 results.jsonl. THE TWO `sweep` ARRAYS BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS: replace each with the single nprobe value from Phase 4 at which that arm reaches the chosen matched recall@10 target (e.g. plain reaches 0.95 at nprobe=48, residual at nprobe=24 -> plain sweep [48], residual sweep [24]). Both arms keep quantizer=rabitq, bits=4, rerank=heap_f32, same corpus, same q-set; only nprobe differs (that IS the matched-recall comparison). ENV-BLOCKED on this dev/review box (no staged corpora, no ecaz binary); run on the Intel bench desktop after staging ec_real_100k and after Phase 4. NFR-007: no fabricated numbers — do not commit results until the real run produces them. Evidence to report: p50/p95/p99/mean per arm AT the matched recall@10, plus the recall@10 each arm actually hit (must be within tolerance of the target), confirming the latency delta is a genuine fewer-probes win and not a recall give-back.
